turns.user:
When the request calls for alternatives, present a brief, context, a portfolio, selected details, connections, and continuation choices. Target 10 to 15 possibilities, subject to the user's constraints and output budget. For each, give a name, mechanism, intended value, category, method label, main uncertainty, and fit note. Develop five to seven selected possibilities if space permits. Answer other requests directly.

Quick mode. Invent a device that continuously cools a sealed, perfectly insulated box while all equipment and energy remain inside it. The box has no heat transfer to its environment, no matter exchange, no stored cold reservoir, no other energy sink and no permitted temperature increase anywhere inside. Preserve every constraint exactly. No experiments.
turns.assistant:
No such device can exist under those constraints.

A continuously cooling sealed, perfectly insulated box must remove heat from its interior. But with:

- no heat transfer outward,
- no mass exchange,
- no stored cold reservoir,
- no internal energy sink,
- no temperature increase anywhere inside,

there is nowhere for the removed energy to go. Any internal refrigeration cycle merely moves heat and ultimately returns the same energy plus its work as additional heat.

This violates conservation of energy—and, for continuous operation, the second law of thermodynamics as well. At most, the box could cool temporarily by consuming a finite internal energy source or warming another internal component, both explicitly forbidden.
